memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They made the robe of the ephod entirely of blue cloth - the work of a weaver - with an opening in the centre of the robe like the opening of a collar, and a band round this opening, so that it would not tear." - Exod 39:22-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A woven band around the neck opening, for one stated reason: so that it would not tear.

The opening was the weak point. Every time the robe was pulled over the priest's head, stress went straight to that seam. So God specified reinforcement exactly there.

We each have a place like that. A besetting temptation. A relationship that always strains us. A time of day or a set of circumstances where we consistently fail. If we are honest, we know where our robe tears.

The wise response is not to pretend the weak point does not exist, and not to despair over it, but to reinforce it deliberately. Paul says to put on the full armour of God so that we can stand against the devil's schemes (Eph 6:11) — schemes implies targeting, and targeting implies known weak spots.

Practically, reinforcement might mean removing an app, changing a route home, telling a trusted friend, deciding in advance what you will do, or refusing to be in a certain situation alone.

Notice the reinforcement was woven in during manufacture, not added after the first tear. God does not want us waiting for the failure before we act.

Where does your robe tear? Strengthen it before you need it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where is the weak point in your character that repeatedly gives way?
2. What practical reinforcement could you put in place this week?
3. Who could you tell, so you are not guarding that point alone?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You know exactly where I am weakest. Strengthen me there before I fail again. Amen.
